# Cyber Web City Spinner

Copyright 2026 Gregg Tavares. Distributed under the adjacent MIT license. Source: [greggman/cyber-web-city](https://github.com/greggman/cyber-web-city), `src/car/spinner.ts`, `src/car/parts.ts`, `src/nurbs/model.ts` and `src/nurbs/tessellate.ts`. Local source snapshot 0f66ac6.

The two compressed mesh files preserve the original position, normal, UV, surface material, and index buffers produced by `buildModelMesh(buildSpinner(), lod)` with the game's own detail settings. `spinner-player.bin.gz` uses `lod = 1` (51,909 solid and glass triangles across 198 modeled parts). `spinner-traffic.bin.gz` uses `lod = 3` (7,160 triangles across the same parts). Glow-volume triangles are additional. Each file begins with six little-endian unsigned integers: magic 0x31435753, vertex count, material count, opaque, glass and glow index counts. The original packed vertex, material, and index arrays follow in that order.

The renderer converts the original forward direction to the Manhattan simulation's +Z direction. Materials, cockpit screens, exhaust illumination and the six civilian colorways follow the source model and shaders. Air traffic adapts the motion in Cyber Web City src/city/traffic.ts and src/shaders/traffic.wgsl: origin + direction × ((initial distance + speed × time) modulo lane length). Opposite directions have separate lanes. The source’s five 60–400 m levels serve the skyline, and additional lower lanes are visible from the street. The Manhattan street directions and collision footprints determine which flight intervals are clear. The upper lanes apply the six sine terms in src/city/warp.ts at the source's gentle 0.25 bend strength, with the offset measured from the Manhattan lane anchor. All craft use the original 0.6 m hover bob and face their path tangent. The head- and taillight batch follows the source lamps' direction and motion-relative shutter. Driver eye position in the converted local coordinates is (0.4, 1.3, 0.05) meters.
